notes: The official USMLE Content Outline (2026) was inspected directly at Skin & Subcutaneous Tissue page 14 and explicitly lists hidradenitis suppurativa.
Current NIAMS pages were used for the target diagnosis and morphology/location pattern.
Current MedlinePlus/NIAMS pages were used for furunculosis, folliculitis, epidermoid-cyst, and nodular-acne distractors.

blueprint.competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
official_outline_path: disorders of sweat and sebaceous glands

option_audit.furunculosis: Real recurrent purulent follicular infection, but does not best explain chronic bilateral intertriginous communicating tunnels and scars.
option_audit.folliculitis: Superficial follicular pustules do not fit deep tunnel-forming disease.
option_audit.epidermoid_cysts: Usually discrete slow-growing cysts rather than a symmetric recurrent tunnel-and-scar pattern.
option_audit.nodular_acne: Can cause deep nodules and scarring but the axillary/inguinal tunnel phenotype is characteristic of HS.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Years of recurrent deep painful nodules in bilateral axillae and groin with draining openings that communicate under the skin and leave scars independently reconstruct hidradenitis suppurativa.
adversarial_second_pass.furunculosis_attack: Recurrent boils are plausible but lack the characteristic chronic interconnected tunnels and stereotyped intertriginous distribution.
adversarial_second_pass.acne_attack: Deep acne nodules may scar, but the stated distribution and sinus-like tunnels make HS uniquely better.
adversarial_second_pass.cueing_attack: The stem does not use the diagnostic label or 'acne inversa'; morphology and distribution must be integrated.
adversarial_second_pass.unsupported_precision_check: No stage, lesion count threshold, treatment regimen, recurrence percentage, or risk-factor magnitude is asserted.
